title: Migrating from closed to open source models, Together
gist: Together AI lays out a five-stage playbook (Discover, Evaluate, Adapt, Decide, Production) for moving enterprise workloads from closed to open source models, arguing the migration takes weeks to months rather than months to years because harnesses, gateways and tooling are already model-agnostic. Key claims: up to 70 percent cost reduction in some cases, real-traffic replay beats public benchmarks, frontier open models often work out of the box, and canary rollouts starting at 10 percent of traffic de-risk the cutover.

insights.claim: Migrating from closed source to open source models breaks the tradition of slow and painful enterprise migration, especially when a managed service absorbs the complexity of keeping pace with AI innovation.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: If migration friction is genuinely low, closed-model incumbents have weaker switching-cost protection than assumed.
insights.quote: closed to open source breaks the tradition of slow and painful migration, especially if you adopt a managed service

insights.claim: A closed-to-open model migration can take weeks to months rather than the months to years typical of traditional technical migrations.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Compresses the window in which closed-model revenue can be considered sticky.
insights.quote: This can take weeks to months rather than months to years.
insights.locator: We'll walk you through a successful migration strategy

insights.claim: Customers have seen up to 70 percent cost reduction in some cases when transitioning to open source models.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: A headline savings figure that, if replicable, pressures per-token pricing across the closed-model market.
insights.quote: We see in some cases up to 70% cost reduction when customers transition to open source.

insights.claim: The blast radius of this migration is much smaller than a traditional one because harnesses, gateways, and tooling are all built to adopt a variety of models, so the technical stack that must change is less complex.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Model-agnostic middleware is the structural reason model providers face commoditization pressure.
insights.quote: Harnesses, gateways, and tooling are all built to adopt a variety of models.

insights.claim: ROI should be quantified out of the evaluation stage as tokens generated per dollar compared against closed source, and the same comparison can be run for quality.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Tokens per dollar is becoming the standard unit of account for inference procurement decisions.
insights.quote: How many tokens can you generate per dollar? How does that compare to closed source?

themes.theme: Discover: benchmark filtering and model tiers

insights.claim: No single model is best across the board, since different models have different strengths across domains, so shortlisting depends on first defining the use-case, workload, and what a good response looks like in plain terms.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Fragmented model strengths favor multi-model platforms and routing layers over single-vendor standardization.
insights.quote: No single model is the best across the board.

insights.claim: Pre-existing benchmarks are useful only as a filtering tool, with cited sources including The Open Frontier, Artificial Analysis, Epoch AI, Vals AI, Scale's leaderboards, Intelligence and Arena.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Identifies which third-party evaluation properties enterprises actually consult when making model buying decisions.
insights.quote: Good sources of benchmarks include The Open Frontier, Artificial Analysis, Epoch AI, Vals AI, Scale's leaderboards, Intelligence and Arena.

insights.claim: Benchmarks are mapped to workload type: FrontierCode, DeepSWE and Terminal Bench 4 for coding agents; LMArena and the AA-Intelligence Index for chat and general assistant work; tau-bench and Agent Arena for agents and tool use; and Vision Arena for vision.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Workload-to-benchmark mapping reveals which eval brands are becoming procurement standards per category.
insights.quote: Coding agents: FrontierCode, DeepSWE, Terminal Bench 4

insights.claim: The open model market is described as three tiers to pick from: Frontier Open such as GLM-5.3 and Kimi K3, Value Tier such as DeepSeek-V4 Flash and GLM-5.3 Flash, and Small and edge-deployable such as Qwen 3.8 27B and Muse Glimmer.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: A tiering model showing Chinese-origin open weights occupying both the frontier and value tiers of enterprise shortlists.
insights.quote: Frontier Open (eg. GLM-5.3, Kimi K3), Value Tier (eg. DeepSeek-V4 Flash, GLM-5.3 Flash), Small and edge-deployable (eg. Qwen 3.8 27B, Muse Glimmer)

insights.claim: Model selection should go beyond raw performance to cost per task, tokens burned per attempt, steps needed, end-to-end runtime, and how quickly a correct answer can be verified, metrics that new benchmarks increasingly report.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Shifts the competitive metric from capability scores to task-level efficiency, which favors smaller efficient models.
insights.quote: Look at cost per task, how many tokens a model burns per attempt, how many steps it needs, end-to-end runtime, and how quickly you can verify a correct answer.

insights.claim: A model that scores a few points lower on benchmarks but completes tasks in half the tokens and half the time may be the better fit.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Undercuts leaderboard-driven purchasing and supports the economics of efficient mid-tier models.
insights.quote: A model that scores a few points lower but completes tasks in half the tokens and half the time may be the better fit.

insights.claim: Before serious evaluation, teams should take representative tasks into a playground, watch for failure modes, and ask whether it is the model failing or the harness and context around it, exiting the step with two to three candidate models.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Attributing failures to harness rather than model changes where engineering budget and vendor blame land.
insights.quote: Watch for failure modes and ask whether it's the model failing or the harness and context around it.

themes.theme: Evaluate: replay real traffic over generic benchmarks

insights.claim: Evaluation splits into accuracy, meaning what the model can do regardless of where it runs or how fast it is, and performance, meaning whether it meets the cost and user-feel or latency expectations needed for adoption.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: A clean two-axis rubric that separates model capability risk from infrastructure and serving risk.
insights.quote: Accuracy defines the capabilities of the model.

insights.claim: Benchmarks are only directionally useful and true tests are done with real data, because workloads have different traffic shapes, niche response requirements, and request structures that no benchmark can represent.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Argues public leaderboards systematically mis-rank models for any specific enterprise workload.
insights.quote: benchmarks are directionally useful, true tests are done with real data

insights.claim: For teams already using closed source models, a simple replay of existing traffic is all the data needed to benchmark alternatives, with no custom suites and no large dataset required.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Removes the data-collection excuse for not testing alternatives, lowering the barrier to switching vendors.
insights.quote: a simple replay of existing traffic is all the data you need to benchmark. No custom suites, no large data set.

insights.claim: Traffic replay is framed as the long-standing best practice for benchmarking systems, predating modern frontier models and used in HPC, databases, and load balancing.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Positions AI evaluation as a normal systems-engineering discipline rather than a novel problem.
insights.quote: This is, and always has been, the best way to bench even before we were benchmarking modern frontier models (HPC, databases, load balancing, etc).

insights.claim: Teams without replayable data can still size against general usage patterns such as input and output size and expected cache hit rate, and gateways like LiteLLM can gather this information when closed source providers do not provide these metrics.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Closed providers withholding usage telemetry is itself a lock-in mechanism that gateway software neutralizes.
insights.quote: If closed source providers don't provide these metrics, gateways like LiteLLM can help gather this information.

insights.claim: Rerunning existing data against candidate models establishes a goal line on cost, speed, or quality, and passing it constitutes technical validation to move on to full-scale migration.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Defines an explicit, auditable decision gate that makes vendor switching a repeatable process rather than a one-off project.
insights.quote: When OSMs pass this goal line you have technical validation and you can move on to a full scale migration.

insights.claim: Investing in robust evaluation techniques enables a team to rapidly adopt new open source models with ease going forward, turning evaluation infrastructure into a durable capability rather than a one-time cost.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Once eval infrastructure exists, model swapping becomes cheap and recurring, accelerating commoditization.
insights.quote: Investing in robust evaluation techniques will enable your team to rapidly adopt new OSMs with ease moving forward.

themes.theme: Adapt: tuning debt lives in the harness, not the model

insights.claim: Frontier open models are getting good enough that they typically work out of the box for most applications.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: A capability-parity claim that, if accurate, removes the main technical objection to open model adoption.
insights.quote: Frontier open models are getting good enough that they typically work out of the box for most applications

insights.claim: When an open model fails evals it usually means the prompt, sampling parameters, and harness were tuned for a different model, because a closed-source setup carries a lot of accumulated tuning the open source model has never seen.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Reframes apparent open-model underperformance as transferable configuration debt rather than a capability gap.
insights.quote: Your closed-source setup carries a lot of accumulated tuning that the open source model has never seen

insights.claim: Adaptation levers are ordered by effort: system prompt engineering, model inference settings such as temperature, top_k, preserved thinking and reasoning effort, context engineering and the harness including skills, tools and MCP servers, and finally model weights via fine-tuning or distillation.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: An effort-ranked ladder that tells buyers where engineering spend goes when adopting open weights.
insights.quote: Context engineering and the harness itself: the skills, tools, and MCP servers that make up the software environment the model operates in.

insights.claim: Fine-tuning or distillation is the hardest lever because it requires well-defined evals, curated data, and real experimentation, but it can unlock a niche domain and make a small model punch well above its weight.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Explains the conditions under which small specialized models displace large general ones in production.
insights.quote: it can unlock a niche domain and make a small model punch well above its weight

insights.claim: Adaptation must be run as an iterative loop with experiments that isolate a single modification, because changing too many variables at once makes it impossible to identify what is working amid confounding noise.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Disciplined experimentation is the operational bottleneck, implying demand for eval and experiment tooling.
insights.quote: If you're testing too many things and changing too many variables at once, you'll never isolate what's working amongst the confounding noise.

themes.theme: Decide and Production: organizational, not technical, friction

insights.claim: Technical validation is only half the battle; results must be packaged and the why communicated to stakeholders with effort, risks, and ROI spelled out.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Sales cycles for open model adoption are gated by internal governance, which lengthens realized revenue timing.
insights.quote: Technical validation is half the battle, as with any migration.

insights.claim: Compatibility concerns for harnesses and tooling still occur occasionally but the gap gets smaller every day, and a tool called togetherlink is provided that is a simple install for using open source models within any harness.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: A drop-in compatibility shim is how a managed provider converts a technical migration into a procurement decision.
insights.quote: togetherlink, a tool we provide makes it a simple install to start utilizing OSMs within any harness

insights.claim: Risks of adopting open source models are the traditional new-technology risks of compliance, scale, continued migration, tooling familiarity and downstream service impact, and a majority of these are addressed by managed providers.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Risk transfer is the core value proposition managed inference providers sell against self-hosting.
insights.quote: A majority of these are addressed by managed providers if you choose to use one.

insights.claim: Once effort, risks and ROI are defined, adoption becomes more about education than technical boundaries.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Implies the remaining moat for closed model vendors is enterprise familiarity and perception, not technology.
insights.quote: Adoption at this point is more about education than technical boundaries.

insights.claim: Moving to production after a closed-to-open source model migration is one of the lightest steps, rather than the long, drawn-out process traditional migrations require.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Inverts the usual assumption that production cutover is the risky phase, supporting fast adoption curves.
insights.quote: with transitioning from closed to OSM, we find this is actually one of the lightest steps

insights.claim: Canary deployments starting with 10 percent of traffic routed to open source have seen great success in validating against production use cases, so the shift does not need to be immediate.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Gradual traffic shifting means closed-model revenue erodes incrementally rather than in visible step changes.
insights.quote: Canary deployments have seen great success with our customers to validate against production use cases, starting with 10% of traffic to open source.

insights.claim: The technical implementation of adopting an open source model can be as simple as switching out an endpoint.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: API-compatible endpoints are the mechanism converting model choice into a pure price-performance decision.
insights.quote: the technical implementation can be as simple as switching out an endpoint!

insights.claim: The authors say they have seen this transition dozens of times with their largest customers and feel strongly it is far less cumbersome than a traditional technical migration.
insights.speaker: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
insights.so_what: Claimed repetition across large accounts is the strongest evidence offered that open model migration is already happening at scale.
insights.quote: we've seen this transition dozens of times with our largest customers and feel strongly that it's far less cumbersome than a traditional technical migration

source_meta.author: Kareem Abdol-Hamid, Zain Hasan, Sonny Khan
